title: AntiPaSTO: Self-Supervised Honesty Steering via Anti-Parallel Representations
entrypoint: nbs/train.py gemma1b-24gb (training) + nbs/eval_baseline_prompting.py / nbs/eval_baseline_repeng.py (baselines) -> antipasto/eval.py + antipasto/metrics.py (Steering F1 table)
primary_claim: AntiPaSTO, a gradient-optimized self-supervised steering method trained only on two contrastive words, achieves a Steering F1 of 31.2 on Gemma-3-1B for honesty steering on out-of-distribution moral dilemmas, versus 4.5 for prompting and 0.0 for arithmetic mean-difference steering (ActAdd/RepEng).
quote: AntiPaSTO on Gemma 3 1B achieves a Steering F1 of 31.2, beating the prompting baseline of 4.5.
tolerance_rationale: headline is a compound of 5 numbers; compare the components by hand
budget_override_reason: README states ~1 h to train one adapter on Gemma-3-1B; the plan runs 3 seeds plus baselines. The inspector's 'minutes' referred to eval only.
inspector_notes: Cleanest repo in this batch: the repo literally ships a config preset named for a 24GB GPU running exactly the headline model (Gemma-3-1B). One historical use of GPT-4o-mini (nbs/eval_baseline_prompting_engineered.py) only generated a fixed prompt string once, back in 2024 -- that text is now hardcoded in the repo, so no live API call is needed to reproduce the table.
headline_artifact: README Results table (Steer F1 by method) reproduced by antipasto/metrics.py::compute_steering_f1, called from antipasto/train/daily_dilemas.py and the nbs/eval_baseline_*.py scripts
